items.entity: square design domain of Fig. 6a (side length)
items.description: Sec. 4.1.1 says only 'square plate ... as shown in Fig. (6a)'. Sec. 4.1 says 'The length is fixed at L = 1.0 m', but only the figure shows which dimension L labels (the side, or a multiple of it). This matters because ℓ = 0.008 and h_min/h_max are absolute lengths, so the side length sets their size relative to the domain.

items.entity: clamped boundary Γ_u of the square plate
items.description: Sec. 4.1.1: 'being fixed at Γ_u as shown in Fig. (6a)'. The text only says u = 0 on Γ_u. It does not say which edge(s) are fixed, or whether the whole edge or only part of it is fixed.
readings: whole left edge clamped (x = 0, 0 ≤ y ≤ L)
whole top edge clamped (y = L, 0 ≤ x ≤ L)
only the central part of the left edge clamped (0.25L ≤ y ≤ 0.75L)
two short clamped segments (≈0.05L each) at the bottom-left and bottom-right corners

items.description: Sec. 4.1.1 says only 'asymmetrically loaded square plate'. The position of Γ_t is shown only in Fig. 6a. Mid-edge positions that would make the problem symmetric are excluded.
readings: lower end of the right edge (bottom-right corner, y ≈ 0), with the left edge clamped
off-centre on the bottom edge at x ≈ 0.75L, with the top edge clamped
on the right edge centred at y = 0.25L
upper end of the right edge (top-right corner, y ≈ L)

items.entity: length/distribution of the loaded segment Γ_t
items.description: Sec. 4.1 gives a traction |t| in N/m that is integrated over Γ_t, so the load is spread along a segment. The segment length, and whether it is really a point load, is never stated in the text.
readings: uniform traction over a segment of length 0.02L
uniform traction over a segment of length 0.05L
uniform traction over a segment of length 0.1L
concentrated load at a single node/corner

items.description: Sec. 4.1 gives only the magnitude |t| = 1.0e3 N/m. The direction is shown only in Fig. 6a. Flipping the sign of the load does not change a linear compliance optimum.

Only the traction density |t| = 1.0e3 N/m is given (Sec. 4.1). The total force depends on the unknown length of Γ_t. The unit N/m could also be read as a point force per unit thickness. A grid solver needs actual nodal forces.
readings: distributed 1.0e3 N/m over a 0.05 m segment: resultant 50 N
distributed 1.0e3 N/m over a 0.1 m segment: resultant 100 N
concentrated force of 1.0e3 N (per unit thickness) at one node

items.entity: level-set Dirichlet condition (forced solid) on the loaded boundary 𝒢_t
items.description: Eq. (2.2), the Sec. 3 discrete system and the A.1 evolution problem set φ = 1 on 𝒢_t, which keeps the load boundary solid. But the A.1 weak form of the standard wave equation, the scheme used in Sec. 4.1.1, sets φ_{v+1} = 0 on 𝒢_t. The text also does not say how thick a passive solid zone this means on a grid.
readings: φ = 1 on Γ_t: passive solid elements along the loaded segment (e.g. one element layer)
φ = 0 on Γ_t: loaded edge held on the interface (Θ = 0.5, τ ≈ 0.125), no solid enforced
no passive/Dirichlet constraint at the load (whole domain designable)

items.entity: 2D elasticity assumption (plane strain vs plane stress)
items.description: Sec. 2.1 gives the Lamé constants 'in plane strain assumption'. Sec. 4.1 does not restate the 2D assumption, while Sec. 4.3 explicitly switches to plane stress for its example. Grid solvers usually default to plane stress.

items.entity: Ersatz stiffness interpolation τ(Θ) and its derivative
items.description: Eq. (40) uses τ = (1−e)Θ^q + e with q = 3. Eq. (41) then sets ∂τ/∂Θ = q(1−e)Θ using Θ^q ≡ Θ, which holds only for a 0/1 Θ. Numerically, Θ is the smooth tanh of Eq. (23). So the penalisation actually used and whether the gradient is consistent are ambiguous.
readings: as written: τ = (1−e)Θ³ + e in the state equation, ∂τ/∂Θ = 3(1−e)Θ

items.entity: finite-element mesh resolution and element type
items.description: Sec. 4.1: element size 'ranges from h_min = 5e-4 to h_max = 1.0e-2' (no units, presumably m), with mmg adaptive remeshing in FreeFEM++. No uniform resolution and no element type/order are given (Sec. 3 mentions only 'order α = 2'). A structured grid must pick one h, and ℓ = 0.008 is smaller than h_max.

items.entity: regularisation / filter radius on the target grid solver
items.description: The only regularisation in Sec. 4.1.1 is the wave-equation parameter ℓ = 0.008 (a length) in the implicit level-set update (A.1). No density or sensitivity filter radius is given, and the text does not say how ℓ maps onto one.
readings: implement the A.1 wave-equation level-set update on the grid with ℓ = 0.008 m and no extra filter
Helmholtz/PDE filter with length parameter 0.008 m

items.description: Sec. 4.1.1 says β is 'varied between β = 2.0 and β = 8.0'. The individual values behind Fig. 7 are not listed. β sets the tanh width and also scales the driving term S_v = f_v β / C_v.

Sec. 4.1 says r 'is increased in each iteration until it reaches a limit value r_max'. The initial λ, initial r, growth rule and r_max are never given. The text also does not say how λ is scaled against the strain-energy sensitivity.

items.entity: normalisation factor C_v of the perturbation term
items.description: Eq. (44) writes C_v = 1/(c_f V0) ∫_D |∂R/∂Θ|_{L²(D)} dΩ with c_f = 1, which integrates a norm over D. The exact definition is therefore unclear, as is whether it is recomputed every iteration. C_v sets the update step size.
readings: C_v = (1/(c_f V0)) ∫_D |∂R/∂Θ| dΩ (mean absolute value), every iteration
C_v = sqrt((1/V0) ∫_D (∂R/∂Θ)² dΩ) / c_f (RMS), every iteration
C_v computed once from the initial full design and kept fixed

items.entity: stopping criterion / maximum number of iterations
items.description: Sec. 3: the loop stops 'if convergence to a minimum is achieved, or a predefined number of iterations is reached'. No tolerance or iteration count is given for Sec. 4.1.1 / Fig. 7.
readings: stop when the relative change in J is < 1e-4 and |G| < 1e-3

items.description: Sec. 4.1: 'a completely filled design domain serves as the initial configuration for both φ0 and φ−1'. The value of φ is not given. In the second-order wave update, the starting amplitude changes how far φ must move before holes appear.
readings: φ0 = φ−1 = 1 everywhere (upper bound of φ)

items.entity: bounding of φ during the update
items.description: Sec. 2.1 defines φ in [−1, 1], but neither the Sec. 3 update scheme nor A.1 says whether φ is clipped to that range after each step. Re-initialisation is said to be unnecessary.
readings: clip φ to [−1, 1] after every update
